title: Metro Line 12 Crawls for Hours After Track-Zone Fault Between Mixcoac and Tláhuac
detail: Mexico City's Sistema de Transporte Colectivo (STC) Metro Line 12 operated at reduced speed along its entire Mixcoac–Tláhuac route from around midday on September 23 after technical staff flagged a fault in the track-control system near the Tláhuac–Tlaltenco interstation, with a probable fiber-optic cut suspected; STC said only that a 'revisión en zona de vías' was underway and that trains were running slow while crews worked to normalize service. Concurrent rainfall-related safety protocols also slowed Metrobús Lines 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, A, and B. Riders reported waits of over 40 minutes and overcrowded platforms during the afternoon commute; STC deployed empty trains to relieve saturated stations. STC said no station closures were planned and denied social-media claims of a multi-day shutdown between September 25 and October 5.

media.caption: Metro Line 12 riders faced delays over 40 minutes after a track-zone fault between Mixcoac and Tláhuac
